video_title: Windy DOES NOT Understand The Jonathan Kuminga Discourse

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The intense media focus on Jonathan Kuminga's contract situation
quotes.excerpt: the amount of attention and coverage that is paid to Jonathan Kuminga's contractual situation, I cannot compute it.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I have nothing against Jonathan Kuminga as a player, but the outside interest in what happens to him is mind-boggling to me. The amount of attention and coverage that is paid to Jonathan Kuminga's contractual situation, I cannot compute it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: The first BonTemps deal, this is the BonTemps podcast today.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: I mean, I'm seeing all these Peyton Watson sign-and-trade scenarios and I'm thinking, stop. You know, apron.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Atlanta Hawks' roster constraints regarding trade flexibility
quotes.excerpt: The Atlanta Hawks have 17 players on their roster with guaranteed contracts. I should say 16.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Atlanta Hawks have 17 players on their roster with guaranteed contracts. I should say 16, right? You said that?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: 16 guarantees, one partial, or one non-guarantee.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Who are they taking in a sign-and-trade for Jonathan Kuminga?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Well, and here's the other thing: they're not going into the luxury tax to do it either. They're 4.1 million below the luxury tax. They aren't going in. So if you're the Lakers and you think you're going to trade them Jarred Vanderbilt, remember, when you sign-and-trade a player and you're taking salary back, it's not like you're getting money off your books.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential free agency and sign-and-trade limitations
quotes.excerpt: if LeBron chooses not to go to Cleveland, I'm seeing, oh, Kuminga, seven years, 645 million, Hall of Fame.
quotes.quote: If LeBron chooses not to go to Cleveland, I'm seeing, oh, Kuminga, seven years, 645 million, Hall of Fame. I'm like, you guys understand that the Cavs, if they take a player in a sign-and-trade, they're hard-capped to the first apron. They can't do that. They're going to spend past the first apron. So, I mean, again, it's one thing if you're like, yeah, we're going to try to acquire Nikola Jokic and like it doesn't work on the cap, okay, maybe you figure that out. I've just never seen anything like it in my career, the intense desire to acquire Jonathan Kuminga at any cost.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's long-standing fascination with Jonathan Kuminga's potential
quotes.excerpt: because we've been talking about him for so long, like we, I mean as the NBA, we've just been talking about Kuminga
quotes.quote: It's just the fascination, Windy, because we've been talking about him for so long, like we, I mean as the NBA, we've just been talking about Kuminga from the moment he got drafted. The two-timeline stuff, playing for the Warriors, like there's just a fascination with him. And he's been productive, right? He's been productive, and then when you're productive, people want to see, oh, he's going to be fully unleashed when he goes to place X. He was supposed to be fully unleashed in Atlanta.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' missed window to acquire Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: the Lakers could actually have done a sign-and-trade for Kuminga two weeks ago.
quotes.quote: If I'm not mistaken, Bobby, the Lakers could actually have done a sign-and-trade for Kuminga two weeks ago. When the Lakers traded Deandre Ayton to the Wizards, there was a window there where the Hawks could have gotten in on the sign-and-trade before the Hawks made other acquisitions and got up against the luxury tax, before they did Lou Dort, maybe even before they did Aaron Wiggins. There was a window for the Lakers to do a deal to get Jonathan Kuminga, but what they could have paid him would have been less than the mid-level.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: The current state of sign-and-trade creativity in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: the creativity of a sign-and-trade right now where 23 teams are basically hard-capped at either the first or second apron
quotes.quote: The window for sign-and-trades, I mean everyone's, outside of LeBron and some other things, like business is pretty much done in the league. I mean there really are, you know, I know the restricted guys are still out there with Lou Dort and Aaron Wiggins, but the creativity of a sign-and-trade right now where 23 teams are basically hard-capped at either the first or second apron, like it's not. And then we mention, and then we take the Atlanta party into it, right? Don't forget about them. They just made this trade and took on 6 million more, and they've got 17 players on their roster. They're not taking back another salary here.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's potential to sign for the minimum and earn a max later
quotes.excerpt: Kuminga might sign somewhere for the minimum, average 20 and 10, and then a year from now, get a max
quotes.quote: Kuminga might sign somewhere for the minimum, average 20 and 10, and then a year from now, get a max for all I know. And maybe that's why he didn't want to take a sub-mid-level offer from the Lakers in that sign-and-trade. I'm not saying it's a bad decision. Just know that that was the window to get to LA was when they sent Ayton to Washington. And by the way, after they sent Ayton to Washington, they then went out and signed Zaccharie Risacher, a wing. So like, and I'm not saying Zaccharie Risacher is better than Kuminga, but they they moved on and signed a wing.
